environment.description: IoT message ingestion service on same EC2 instance, but origin is fronted by CloudFront distribution (d1234abcdef.cloudfront.net) with a custom origin access configuration. The origin's security group restricts inbound to the AWS CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing) only. The CloudFront distribution has a custom cache behavior on POST /messages/* with Trusted Key Group signer (key group kg-iot-prod-2024) requiring Ed25519 signed URLs with 30-second expiry. CloudFront's origin request policy forwards Content-Type and X-Device-Auth headers only. The CloudFront distribution has a field-level encryption profile (fle-profile-iot-msg) applied to the 'device_id' field in POST bodies, which re-encodes the device_id value using RSA-OAEP before forwarding to origin — meaning the regex processes the encrypted ciphertext (base64 string) rather than attacker-controlled raw input. Additionally, the distribution has a response timeout of 10 seconds and connection timeout of 5 seconds to origin.

config.origin_access: Security group limited to com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing prefix list
config.signed_urls: Trusted Key Group kg-iot-prod-2024, Ed25519, 30s expiry
config.field_level_encryption: Profile fle-profile-iot-msg encrypts 'device_id' field with RSA-OAEP before forwarding to origin
config.direct_origin_access: blocked by security group - only CloudFront prefix list allowed
